scope: Temporary SQLite files only; no product writer or user database

mechanism.connectionOwner: Windows PowerShell 5.1 process using P/Invoke into winsqlite3.dll, with the loaded DLL path checked against the Windows system directory
mechanism.open: sqlite3_open_v2(SQLITE_OPEN_READWRITE) opens an existing temporary main DB without CREATE
mechanism.openedFileIdentity: sqlite3_file_control(db, main, SQLITE_FCNTL_WIN32_GET_HANDLE) obtains the handle from the same SQLite connection's main xOpen file; GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileIdInfo) returns volume serial plus 128-bit file ID
mechanism.comparison: A temporary expected ID retained by the test is mandatory for schema write and compared before sqlite3_exec; missing expectation rejects before SQLite open, and mismatch closes the connection without schema SQL
mechanism.firstWritePosition: Only a matched identity reaches sqlite3_exec(CREATE TABLE probe_marker); the mismatch fixture retains its original bytes and has no resource.sqlite3 sidecar
mechanism.notIdentityEvidence: The File.Exists check limits probe input to an existing OS-temp file; it is not the comparison evidence. No separate guard FD or DatabaseSync(path) is used.

installedShapeObserved.nativeRuntime: OS winsqlite3.dll and Windows PowerShell 5.1; no probe-owned native binary. The loaded DLL path is checked against the Windows system directory before SQLite open, after DLL load.
installedShapeObserved.powershellExecutableObserved: C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe resolved on this host; the runner invokes powershell.exe by name
installedShapeObserved.probeScriptLocation: Copied into an unprotected test temp directory; no signed or protected installation was tested
installedShapeObserved.invocation: Node.js run.mjs starts powershell.exe, which owns the SQLite connection and returns identity/status as JSON

check.observed: 1 test: installed two-file copy without node_modules; empty expected ID blocks schema write; actual main-handle identity stable across reopen; matched identity permits schema write; path replacement changes identity and rejects before schema write; replacement bytes and sidecar list unchanged

unobservedMatrix: Other Windows builds, architectures, PowerShell policy modes and winsqlite3 versions
Linux with Node 22 or 24; the Windows-only probe test skips there
notEstablished: Protected operational expected-ID provenance or writer/worker OS-principal separation

Protected or signed PowerShell executable, probe script and DLL provenance in an operational install; the DLL path check after load is not a defense against worker-controlled replacement or native code execution
Sidecar, alias, restart, crash and adversarial race controls required for a product writer
B14-h/i completion or B14-c schema/admission activation
